papers.title_in_file: PennyLane: Automatic differentiation of hybrid quantum-classical computations
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, derivative and gradient-method sections, Conclusion; code listings and plugin appendices skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: Software-framework paper describing PennyLane, a Python library for differentiable programming of quantum computers.

assertions.value: The authors state that PennyLane's core feature is computing gradients of variational quantum circuits in a way compatible with classical backpropagation, extending automatic differentiation to quantum and hybrid computations.
quotes: PennyLane's core feature is the ability to compute gradients of variational quantum circuits in a way that is compatible with classical techniques such as backpropagation.
PennyLane thus extends the automatic differentiation algorithms common in optimization and machine learning to include quantum and hybrid computations.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' description of their own (Xanadu-led) software; the paper's statement is a self-description.

assertions.value: The paper states that most quantum nodes permit analytic hardware derivatives via parameter-shift rules (used on hardware or on simulators where shots is not None), and that finite differences is applied when the circuit does not permit analytic hardware gradients.
quotes: Most quantum nodes permit analytic derivatives on hardware via parameter-shift rules
Finally, if the circuit does not permit analytic hardware gradients, numerical methods such as the method of finite differences is applied.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' description of the software's documented behavior, not a measured result.

papers.title_in_file: Hardware-efficient variational quantum algorithms for time evolution
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Fig. 1 caption, Discussion; method derivations and appendices not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: Algorithm paper presenting variational time-evolution methods (angle, block and cone update) that avoid matrix inversion, tested numerically on local Hamiltonians.

assertions.value: The authors present alternatives to the time-dependent variational principle that are hardware-efficient and do not require matrix inversion, analyzed numerically on quantum Hamiltonians with local interactions.
quotes: Here we present alternatives to the time-dependent variational principle that are hardware-efficient and do not require matrix inversion.
We numerically analyze the performance of our algorithms using quantum Hamiltonians with local interactions.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' claim backed by numerical simulation on spin-chain Hamiltonians; no hardware run in the passages read.

assertions.value: In the Discussion the authors state that angle update, their most efficient algorithm, performed remarkably well at finding ground states by imaginary time evolution, and that they presented numerical evidence that block and cone update achieve the high accuracy required for real time evolution.
quotes: Our most efficient algorithm, angle update, performed remarkably well at this task.
We presented numerical evidence that block and cone update achieve the high accuracy required.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' summary of simulation results; numerical, not hardware.

papers.title_in_file: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Quantum Technologies
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Contents, Introduction, Sec. II.A, Outlook; Sec. III applications not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: Perspective article surveying selected examples of machine learning applied to quantum technologies.

assertions.value: The authors state that their selection of examples is subjective and that they do not claim a comprehensive list of the literature.
quotes: Our selection is necessarily subjective. We thus make no claim as to providing a comprehensive list of the literature and apologize to anyone who misses some favorite work.
assertions.certainty_reason: Direct statement by the authors about their own review scope.

assertions.value: The authors state, citing another area of work, that modern deep-learning methods can be significantly outperformed by rather simple methods if applied to the wrong task.
quotes: Often, modern deep-learning methods can be significantly outperformed by rather simple methods if applied to the wrong task, as seen in other areas [8].
assertions.certainty_reason: A general remark in a perspective article that rests on one citation; no data shown.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Neuron: an elementary building block for machine learning on quantum computers
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Discussion, parts of the simulation theorem (Theorem 2) and XOR example.
papers.what_it_is: Proposal paper constructing a quantum neuron with threshold activation via repeat-until-success circuits, with numerical simulation of feedforward and Hopfield networks.

assertions.value: The authors state that their quantum neuron model can simulate classical neurons with sigmoid or step function activation while processing inputs in quantum superposition.
quotes: our model is able to simulate classical neurons with sigmoid or step function activation while processing inputs in quantum superposition.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' constructive claim; supported by a stated theorem and numerics in the paper body.

assertions.value: The abstract states numerical evidence that a feedforward network of quantum neurons trained with a superposition of inputs and the corresponding output learns the function, and that this training suffices to learn it on all individual inputs separately.
quotes: we provide numerical evidence that the network not only can learn a function when trained with superposition of inputs and the corresponding output
but that this training suffices to learn the function on all individual inputs separately.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation evidence (small examples such as XOR), as the authors describe it.

assertions.value: The authors show numerically that their model reproduces Hopfield attractor dynamics, converging to a unique memorized pattern even when starting from a quantum superposition of input states.
quotes: we show numerically that our model reproduces the attractor dynamics by converging to a unique, memorized, pattern even when starting from a quantum superposition of input states.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation on small example networks.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Conclusion, start of Appendix A; algorithm sections and proofs not read line by line.
papers.what_it_is: Theory paper giving two quantum algorithms for perceptron training with proven complexity bounds.

assertions.value: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that determines a separating hyperplane in a number of steps sublinear in the number of data points N, which they describe as a quadratic speedup with respect to the size of the training data.
quotes: The first algorithm exploits quantum information processing to determine a separating hyperplane using a number of steps sublinear in the number of data points N
The first provides a quadratic speedup with respect to the size of the training data.
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytic result with proofs in the paper; the speedup is in query count to the training data.

assertions.value: The second algorithm gives a quadratic reduction in the scaling of training time, measured by interactions with the training data, with the margin between the classes, which the authors describe as a quartic speedup relative to typical perceptron training bounds.
quotes: The second provides a quadratic reduction in the scaling of the training time (as measured by the number of interactions with the training data) with the margin between the two classes.
This latter result is especially interesting because it constitutes a quartic speedup relative to the typical perceptron training bounds that are usually seen in the literature.
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytic result with proofs (Theorem 2 and lemmas in the appendix); measured as data-access count.

assertions.value: The authors state that their work demonstrates quantum computing can provide provable speedups for perceptron training.
quotes: Perhaps the most significant feature of our work is that it demonstrates that quantum computing can provide provable speedups for perceptron training, which is a foundational machine learning method.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own summary of significance; the speedups are in oracle or data-access complexity, as the paper scopes them.

papers.title_in_file: Variational quantum unsampling on a quantum photonic processor
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, protocol section, experimental results (Sec. IV), concluding remarks; appendices not read.
papers.what_it_is: Protocol and experimental paper introducing Variational Quantum Unsampling (VQU) and demonstrating it on a quantum photonic processor, with simulations up to six photons.

assertions.value: The authors introduce the Variational Quantum Unsampling protocol, a nonlinear quantum neural network approach for verification and inference of near-term quantum circuit outputs, and state that they experimentally demonstrate it on a quantum photonic processor.
quotes: In this work we introduce the Variational Quantum Unsampling (VQU) protocol, a nonlinear quantum neural network approach for verification and inference of near-term quantum circuits outputs.
Here, we experimentally demonstrate the VQU protocol on a quantum photonic processor.
assertions.certainty_reason: One experimental demonstration on a single photonic chip.

assertions.value: In the experiment the final fidelity, defined as the overlap between the initialization state and output state, was found to be F = 0.695 with an uncertainty of 0.053 (printed with a plus-minus sign), and the authors attribute the noise floor primarily to low signal-to-noise ratio from photon emission by thermo-optic phase shifters and high fiber-to-chip coupling loss.
quotes: The final fidelity of the VQU protocol, defined as the overlap between the initialization state and output state
This noise floor is primarily due to a low signal-to-noise ratio, caused by photon emission from our thermo-optic phase shifters and high fiber-to-chip coupling loss
assertions.certainty_reason: A measured result on one device; the numeric fidelity text contains symbols and is not inside the quoted spans, so the coordinator should check it against the PDF.

assertions.value: Numerical simulations up to six photons suggest to the authors that local optima are limited and unlikely to prevent convergence for optical unsampling experiments.
quotes: The efficiency of these numerical experiments suggest that the presence of local optima are limited and unlikely to prevent convergence for optical unsampling experiments.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' interpretation of simulations up to six photons; not a proof.

papers.title_in_file: Layer VQE: A Variational Approach for Combinatorial Optimization on Noisy Quantum Computers
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Related Work start, Conclusions; numerical-results tables and appendices skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: Algorithm paper proposing iterative Layer VQE (L-VQE) and a qubit-frugal formulation for k-community detection, evaluated by classical simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report numerical comparison of L-VQE with QAOA on multiple-community detection and state that QAOA achieves lower approximation ratios while requiring significantly deeper circuits.
quotes: We numerically compare L-VQE with Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and demonstrate that QAOA achieves lower approximation ratios while requiring significantly deeper circuits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation results on the paper's test graphs for k-communities detection only.

assertions.value: The authors state that L-VQE is more robust to finite sampling errors and has a higher chance of finding the solution than standard VQE approaches.
quotes: We show that L-VQE is more robust to finite sampling errors and has a higher chance of finding the solution as compared with standard VQE approaches.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation on the paper's graph instances, with comparison tables.

assertions.value: The authors state that existing formulations of k-communities modularity maximization require kn qubits for a graph with n nodes, and that their formulation requires only n log k qubits.
assertions.anchor: Sec. I and Conclusions, pp. 2 and 12
quotes: In existing works, for a graph with n nodes, solving the k-communities modularity maximization problem requires kn qubits that encode the problem as an Ising model Hamiltonian.
We propose a novel qubit-frugal formulation that requires only n log k qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' formulation; qubit counts follow their encoding.

assertions.value: The simulations used a matrix product state representation in MATLAB, and a separate study used a simulator of a noisy trapped-ion quantum computer; the results are classical simulation.
quotes: We use matrix product state representation to perform large-scale simulations of the quantum circuits in MATLAB.
We also studied the performance of L-VQE using a simulator of noisy trapped-ion quantum computer.
assertions.certainty_reason: Statement of the study's own method; scope is simulation, not hardware.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract gives up to 40 qubits and 352 parameters as the simulated size; this is not in the quoted spans.

papers.title_in_file: Hamiltonian variational ansatz without barren plateaus
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Conclusion; proofs and numerical sections not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: Theory and numerics paper on gradient scaling in the Hamiltonian variational ansatz (HVA) and a parameter-constrained initialization.

assertions.value: The authors show that a circuit given by a time-evolution operator generated by a local Hamiltonian does not have exponentially small gradients, and derive parameter conditions under which the HVA is well approximated by such an operator.
quotes: After showing that a circuit described by a time-evolution operator generated by a local Hamiltonian does not have exponentially small gradients, we derive parameter conditions for which the HVA is well approximated by such an operator.
assertions.certainty_reason: Rigorous proof for short-time evolution plus numerical evidence for long-time evolution, as the conclusion states.

assertions.value: The conclusion states that for the short-time regime the authors give a rigorous proof, while for long-time evolution the support is numerical evidence based on quantum thermalization, with extensive numerics for up to 28 qubits.
quotes: For the short-time regime, we provided a rigorous proof based on the rate of the gradient evolution, while we showed numerical evidence based on quantum thermalization
We further supported our arguments with extensive numerics for up to 28 qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors distinguish proof (short time) from numerical evidence (long time).

assertions.value: The authors state that the paper did not consider incoherent noise, which prevails in noisy quantum devices, and that how noise strength, circuit depth and initialization schemes interplay requires a separate study.
quotes: This paper did not consider incoherent noise, which prevails in noisy quantum devices.
Still, how the strength of the noise, the circuit depth, and the initialization schemes interplay in general is another big question that requires a separate study.
assertions.certainty_reason: Explicit limitation stated by the authors.
